## Boggart (CR 5)

**XP** 1,600  
 CE Small aberration (air, shapechanger)  
 **Init** +4; **Senses** darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +12  
 

**Defense**

 
 **AC** 21, touch 16, flat-footed 15 (+4 Dex, +1 dodge, +5 natural, +1 size)  
 **hp** 60 (6d8+12)  
 **Fort** +3; **Ref** +6; **Will** +6  
 **Immune** magic  
 

**Offense**

 
 **Speed** 20 ft.  
 **Melee** slam +9 (2d6+3 electricity)  
 **Special Attacks** confusion, electrical discharge, feed  
 **Spell-like Abilities** (CL 1st)  
 
  10/day—invisibility  
 

**Statistics**

 
 **Str** 12, **Dex** 19, **Con** 15, **Int** 14, **Wis** 12, **Cha** 14  
 **Base Atk** +4; **CMB** +7; **CMD** 19  
 **Feats** Alertness, Blind-Fight, [Dodgility](../../rules/feats/dodge.md), [Weapon Finesse](../../rules/feats/weapon-finesse.md)**Skills** Acrobatics +13 (+11 jumping), Bluff +8, Escape Artist +13, Fly +13, Perception +12, Stealth +17  
 **SQ** change shape (boggart, will-o’-wisp, polymorph any object), detect thoughts, invisibility  
 

**Special Abilities**

 
 **Change Shape (Su)** A boggart’s natural form is that of a small humanoid (resembling a young gnome, halfling, or goblin). It has one other form: that of a small, immature will-o’-wisp. In humanoid form, a boggart assumes the same appearance and traits of its form, much as a lycanthrope would. In humanoid form, a boggart retains all of its special attacks and special qualities.
